purpose.title: About Figurio
points: Figurio is a web-based image editor designed for preparing images for academic and technical documents.
It is intended for students, and authors who need to quickly refine screenshots, diagrams, and figures without using complex graphic software.
The editor provides essential tools for cropping, highlighting important areas, removing unwanted elements, adding annotations, and applying presentation frames.
Its focused feature set avoids unnecessary complexity while keeping the workflow fast, clear, and intuitive.
Figurio runs directly in the browser with no installation required.
All image processing is performed locally in the browser, emphasizing privacy, security, and protection of sensitive data.

featureTour.text: A collection of short demonstration videos presenting individual tools and selected advanced features. Each video focuses on a specific functionality and provides a concise explanation of its purpose and usage. The feature tour can be accessed at any time.

technicalLimitations.title: Technical Limitations
limitations: PDF files with complex layouts, or advanced graphical elements may not render exactly as in the original document.
Large image files may affect performance depending on your device, available memory, and browser capabilities.
Animated images (e.g., GIFs) are not supported.
Undo and redo history is limited to preserve performance and memory usage.
Refreshing the browser or closing the tab will discard any unsaved changes.

statistics.title: Statistics
statistics.text: Anonymous usage data is collected to help improve the editor’s functionality, usability, and performance. The collected statistics are aggregated and do not include personal content from edited images. Data reflects how often individual tools and features are used.

userStatistics.title: Usage Statistics
userStatistics.text: Anonymous usage data is collected to help improve the editor’s functionality, usability, and performance. The collected statistics are aggregated and do not include any content from edited images. No part of images leaves the browser. Data reflects how often individual tools and features are used.
